549	
550	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
551	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
552	    source_dataset: str,
553	    source_version: int,
554	    source_field: str,
555	    source_field_id: int,
556	) -> None:
557	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
558	
559	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
560	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
561	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
562	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
563	    """
564	    rows = conn.execute(
565	        """
566	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
567	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
568	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
569	                sv.version         AS source_version,
570	                sf.name            AS source_field
571	        FROM    lineage_links ll
572	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
573	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
574	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
575	        """
576	    ).fetchall()
577	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
578	    for row in rows:
579	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
580	
581	    visited = {source_field_id}
582	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
583	    queue = [source_field_id]
584	    while queue:
585	        current = queue.pop()
586	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
587	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
588	                continue
589	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
590	            upstream.add(
591	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
592	            )
593	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
594	
595	    conn.executemany(
596	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
597	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
598	        sorted(upstream),
599	    )
600	
601	
602	def get_lineage_impact(
603	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version: int, field: str
604	) -> dict:
605	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
606	    _, field_id = _require_field(conn, dataset, version, field, role="Source")
607	
608	    impacted = _impact_cache_lookup(conn, dataset["name"], version, field)
609	    if impacted is None:
610	        impacted = _compute_impacted(conn, field_id)
611	        _impact_cache_store(conn, dataset["name"], version, field, impacted)
612	
613	    return {
614	        "source": {"dataset": dataset["name"], "version": version, "field": field},
615	        "impacted": impacted,
616	    }

649	def _is_finite_number(value: Any) -> bool:
650	    # bool is a subclass of int; a boolean is not a numeric value here.
651	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
652	        return False
653	    return math.isfinite(value)

656	def _validate_rule_params(
657	    kind: str, params: dict[str, Any], field_names: set[str]
658	) -> None:
659	    """Validate rule parameters structurally (422) and against the schema (404)."""
660	
661	    def require_existing_field(field_name: Any) -> str:
662	        if not isinstance(field_name, str) or not field_name:
663	            raise RequestInvalidError(
664	                f"Rule kind '{kind}' requires a non-empty 'field' parameter"
665	            )
666	        if field_name not in field_names:
667	            raise NotFoundError(f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in this version")
668	        return field_name
669	
670	    if kind == "not_null":
671	        require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
672	        return
673	
674	    if kind == "numeric_range":
675	        field_name = require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
676	        minimum = params.get("min")
677	        maximum = params.get("max")
678	        if not _is_finite_number(minimum) or not _is_finite_number(maximum):
679	            raise RequestInvalidError(
680	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires finite numeric 'min' and 'max'"
681	            )
682	        if minimum > maximum:
683	            raise RequestInvalidError(
684	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires min <= max"
685	            )
686	        return
687	
688	    if kind == "unique":
689	        fields = params.get("fields")
690	        if not isinstance(fields, list) or not fields:
691	            raise RequestInvalidError(
692	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires a non-empty 'fields' list"
693	            )
694	        if not all(isinstance(name, str) and name for name in fields):
695	            raise RequestInvalidError(
696	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain non-empty field names"
697	            )
698	        if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
699	            raise RequestInvalidError(
700	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain no duplicates"
701	            )
702	        unknown = [name for name in fields if name not in field_names]
703	        if unknown:
704	            raise NotFoundError(
705	                f"Field '{unknown[0]}' does not exist in this version"
706	            )
707	        return

809	def _row_violates_not_null(row: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> bool:
810	    return field not in row or row[field] is None
811	
812	
813	def _row_violates_numeric_range(
814	    row: dict[str, Any], field: str, minimum: float, maximum: float
815	) -> bool:
816	    if field not in row:
817	        return True
818	    value = row[field]
819	    if value is None or not _is_finite_number(value):
820	        return True
821	    return value < minimum or value > maximum
822	
823	
824	def _row_violates_unique(row: dict[str, Any], fields: list[str]) -> tuple:
825	    return tuple(None if name not in row else row[name] for name in fields)
826	
827	
828	def _json_combo_key(combo: tuple) -> str:
829	    # Values are already JSON-decoded scalars (or nested arrays/objects); use
830	    # JSON text so that, e.g., the number 1 and the string "1" never compare
831	    # equal and nested objects with reordered keys still match.
832	    return json.dumps(combo, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
833	
834	
835	def evaluate_quality_rules(
836	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int, rows: list[dict]
837	) -> dict:
838	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
839	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
840	
841	    rule_rows = conn.execute(
842	        "SELECT id, name, kind, params, enabled "
843	        "FROM quality_rules WHERE version_id = ? AND enabled = 1 ORDER BY id",
844	        (version_row["id"],),
845	    ).fetchall()
846	
847	    results: list[dict] = []
848	    for rule_row in rule_rows:
849	        params = json.loads(rule_row["params"])
850	        kind = rule_row["kind"]
851	        violations: list[int] = []
852	
853	        if kind == "not_null":
854	            field = params["field"]
855	            violations = [
856	                index
857	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
858	                if _row_violates_not_null(row, field)
859	            ]
860	        elif kind == "numeric_range":
861	            field = params["field"]
862	            violations = [
863	                index
864	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
865	                if _row_violates_numeric_range(
866	                    row, field, params["min"], params["max"]
867	                )
868	            ]
869	        elif kind == "unique":
870	            fields = params["fields"]
871	            seen: dict[str, int] = {}
872	            duplicated: set[int] = set()
873	            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
874	                combo = _row_violates_unique(row, fields)
875	                key = _json_combo_key(combo)
876	                if key in seen:
877	                    duplicated.add(seen[key])
878	                    duplicated.add(index)
879	                else:
880	                    seen[key] = index
881	            violations = sorted(duplicated)
882	
883	        results.append(
884	            {
885	                "rule_id": rule_row["id"],
886	                "name": rule_row["name"],
887	                "passed": not violations,
888	                "violations": violations,
889	            }
890	        )
891	
892	    return {
893	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
894	        "version": version_row["version"],
895	        "results": results,
896	    }

1171	def _parse_at_timestamp(raw: str) -> datetime:
1172	    try:
1173	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
1174	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
1175	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1176	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1177	        ) from exc
1178	    # A trailing timezone designator (offset or 'Z') is mandatory.
1179	    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:
1180	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1181	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must include a timezone"
1182	        )
1183	    return parsed

1186	def get_snapshot_at(
1187	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1188	    dataset_name: str,
1189	    version_number: int,
1190	    raw_timestamp: str | None,
1191	) -> dict:
1192	    if raw_timestamp is None or not raw_timestamp:
1193	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1194	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' is required and must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1195	        )
1196	    target = _parse_at_timestamp(raw_timestamp)
1197	
1198	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1199	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1200	
1201	    # Select the newest snapshot chronologically (ties broken by the highest
1202	    # id); comparing parsed instants also handles any offset in the target.
1203	    candidates = conn.execute(
1204	        "SELECT id, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE version_id = ?",
1205	        (version_row["id"],),
1206	    ).fetchall()
1207	    eligible = [
1208	        (datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]), row["id"])
1209	        for row in candidates
1210	        if datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]) <= target
1211	    ]
1212	    if not eligible:
1213	        raise NotFoundError(
1214	            f"No snapshot of version {version_number} of dataset "
1215	            f"'{dataset_name}' exists at or before the requested timestamp"
1216	        )
1217	    match_id = max(eligible, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1]))[1]
1218	
1219	    row = conn.execute(
1220	        "SELECT id, row_count, rows, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE id = ?",
1221	        (match_id,),
1222	    ).fetchone()
1223	    result = _snapshot_metadata(row, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])
1224	    result["rows"] = json.loads(row["rows"])
1225	    return result

1253	) -> tuple[Counter, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:

1255	    examples: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

1258	        counts[key] += 1

1263	def diff_snapshots(
1264	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1265	    dataset_name: str,
1266	    version_number: int,
1267	    from_snapshot_id: int,
1268	    to_snapshot_id: int,
1269	) -> dict:
1270	    # Validate the path target first so unknown dataset/version stay 404.
1271	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1272	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1273	
1274	    from_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, from_snapshot_id)
1275	    if from_row is None:
1276	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {from_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1277	    to_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, to_snapshot_id)
1278	    if to_row is None:
1279	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {to_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1280	
1281	    for row, snapshot_id in ((from_row, from_snapshot_id), (to_row, to_snapshot_id)):
1282	        if row["version_id"] != version_row["id"]:
1283	            raise RequestInvalidError(
1284	                f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not belong to version "
1285	                f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'; snapshots can "
1286	                "only be compared within the same dataset and version"
1287	            )
1288	
1289	    from_rows = json.loads(from_row["rows"])
1290	    to_rows = json.loads(to_row["rows"])
1291	    from_counts, from_examples = _snapshot_multiset(from_rows)
1292	    to_counts, to_examples = _snapshot_multiset(to_rows)
1293	
1294	    added_keys = sorted(key for key in to_counts if to_counts[key] > from_counts[key])
1295	    removed_keys = sorted(key for key in from_counts if from_counts[key] > to_counts[key])
1296	
1297	    return {
1298	        "from_snapshot_id": from_snapshot_id,
1299	        "to_snapshot_id": to_snapshot_id,
1300	        "added": [
1301	            {"row": to_examples[key], "count": to_counts[key] - from_counts[key]}
1302	            for key in added_keys
1303	        ],
1304	        "removed": [
1305	            {"row": from_examples[key], "count": from_counts[key] - to_counts[key]}
1306	            for key in removed_keys
1307	        ],
1308	    }

1356	def _compute_version_field_impacted(
1357	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, version_id: int
1358	) -> list[dict]:
1359	    """Downstream union of every field of one schema version.
1360	
1361	    All of the version's fields seed the same reachability walk, so direct and
1362	    indirect downstream fields are found once, cycles terminate and the version's
1363	    own fields never appear in the result.
1364	    """
1365	    field_rows = conn.execute(
1366	        "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ?", (version_id,)
1367	    ).fetchall()
1368	    seeds = [row["id"] for row in field_rows]
1369	
1370	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
1371	    visited = set(seeds)
1372	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
1373	    queue = list(seeds)
1374	    while queue:
1375	        current = queue.pop()
1376	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
1377	            if target_field_id in visited:
1378	                continue
1379	            visited.add(target_field_id)
1380	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
1381	            queue.append(target_field_id)
1382	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]
1383

1397	def create_snapshot_deletion_request(
1398	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1399	    dataset_name: str,
1400	    version_number: int,
1401	    snapshot_id: int,
1402	    reason: str,
1403	) -> dict:
1404	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1405	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1406	
1407	    clean_reason = reason.strip()
1408	    if not clean_reason:
1409	        raise RequestInvalidError("'reason' must not be empty")
1410	
1411	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1412	    if snapshot_row is None:
1413	        raise NotFoundError(
1414	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not exist in version "
1415	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1416	        )
1417	
1418	    policy_row = conn.execute(
1419	        "SELECT id FROM retention_policies WHERE version_id = ?",
1420	        (version_row["id"],),
1421	    ).fetchone()
1422	    if policy_row is None:
1423	        raise NotFoundError(
1424	            f"No retention policy exists for version {version_number} of "
1425	            f"dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1426	        )
1427	
1428	    open_request = conn.execute(
1429	        "SELECT id FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1430	        "WHERE snapshot_id = ? AND status IN ('pending', 'blocked')",
1431	        (snapshot_id,),
1432	    ).fetchone()
1433	    if open_request is not None:
1434	        raise ConflictError(
1435	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request "
1436	            f"({open_request['id']})"
1437	        )
1438	
1439	    # An active retention exception (version- or snapshot-scoped) forbids
1440	    # opening a deletion request; the check shares this transaction with the
1441	    # insert below, so the two commit atomically.
1442	    _require_no_active_retention_exception(
1443	        conn, version_row, snapshot_id, dataset_name, version_number
1444	    )
1445	
1446	    impacted = _compute_version_field_impacted(conn, version_row["id"])
1447	    status = "blocked" if impacted else "pending"
1448	    try:
1449	        cursor = conn.execute(
1450	            "INSERT INTO snapshot_deletion_requests ("
1451	            "version_id, snapshot_id, policy_id, reason, status, impacted, created_at"
1452	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1453	            (
1454	                version_row["id"],
1455	                snapshot_id,
1456	                policy_row["id"],
1457	                clean_reason,
1458	                status,
1459	                json.dumps(impacted),
1460	                utc_now_iso(),
1461	            ),
1462	        )
1463	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
1464	        # Lost a race against a concurrent open-request insert.
1465	        raise ConflictError(
1466	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request"
1467	        ) from exc
1468	    row = conn.execute(
1469	        "SELECT * FROM snapshot_deletion_requests WHERE id = ?",
1470	        (cursor.lastrowid,),
1471	    ).fetchone()
1472	    return _deletion_request_row_to_dict(row)

1475	def list_snapshot_deletion_requests(
1476	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1477	    dataset_name: str,
1478	    version_number: int,
1479	    snapshot_id: int,
1480	) -> list[dict]:
1481	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1482	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1483	
1484	    # The collection stays addressable after its snapshot has been confirmed
1485	    # away: the snapshot itself may be gone, but its request records remain.
1486	    # A snapshot id that never existed in this version and has no requests is an
1487	    # unknown resource.
1488	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1489	    request_rows = conn.execute(
1490	        "SELECT id FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1491	        "WHERE version_id = ? AND snapshot_id = ?",
1492	        (version_row["id"], snapshot_id),
1493	    ).fetchall()

"""Pydantic models for the dataset, schema-version and lineage APIs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StrictBool, StrictInt, StrictStr


class DatasetCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty dataset name")
    description: str = Field(default="", description="Optional human description")


class Dataset(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    description: str
    created_at: str


class FieldSpec(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty field name within the version")
    type: str = Field(description="Field type, e.g. 'string' or 'integer'")
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersionCreate(BaseModel):
    fields: list[FieldSpec] = Field(description="Non-empty list of field definitions")


class FieldInfo(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    name: str
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersion(BaseModel):
    dataset_id: int
    dataset_name: str
    version: int
    created_at: str
    fields: list[FieldInfo]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Read-only schema version diff
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class FieldChangeDefinition(BaseModel):
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class VersionFieldChange(BaseModel):
    field: str
    kind: Literal["added", "removed", "changed"]
    # Null on the side where the field does not exist; never omitted.
    before: FieldChangeDefinition | None
    after: FieldChangeDefinition | None


class VersionDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    from_version: int
    to_version: int
    compatible: bool
    changes: list[VersionFieldChange]


class LineageCreate(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    target_field: str
    source_dataset: str
    source_version: int
    source_field: str


class LineageSourceRef(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    field: str


class TargetFieldLineage(BaseModel):
    target_field: str
    sources: list[LineageSourceRef]


class LineageCreatedResponse(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    target_field: str
    source: LineageSourceRef


class LineageResponse(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    fields: list[TargetFieldLineage]


class LineageImpactResponse(BaseModel):
    source: LineageSourceRef
    impacted: list[LineageSourceRef]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Quality rules
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


QualityRuleKind = Literal["not_null", "numeric_range", "unique"]


class QualityRuleCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    name: str = Field(description="Unique rule name within the version")
    kind: QualityRuleKind
    params: dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Kind-specific parameters: {'field': ...}, "
        "{'field': ..., 'min': ..., 'max': ...} or {'fields': [...]}",
    )


class QualityRule(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    kind: QualityRuleKind
    params: dict[str, Any]
    enabled: bool
    created_at: str


class QualityRuleEnabledUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    enabled: StrictBool


class QualityRuleEvaluateRequest(BaseModel):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        description="Rows to check; only enabled rules are executed"
    )


class QualityRuleResult(BaseModel):
    rule_id: int
    name: str
    passed: bool
    violations: list[int]


class QualityRuleEvaluateResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    results: list[QualityRuleResult]


class ErrorResponse(BaseModel):
    error: str
    detail: str | None = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Privacy policies
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


PrivacyMasking = Literal["redact", "partial"]


class PrivacyPolicyCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    field: StrictStr = Field(description="Existing field of the schema version")
    classification: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty sensitivity classification")
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    allowed_roles: list[StrictStr] = Field(
        description="Distinct, non-empty role names that see the raw value; may be empty"
    )


class PrivacyPolicy(BaseModel):
    id: int
    field: str
    classification: str
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    allowed_roles: list[str]
    enabled: bool
    created_at: str


class PrivacyPolicyEnabledUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    enabled: StrictBool


class PrivacyViewRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    role: StrictStr
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


class PrivacyViewResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Row snapshots
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class SnapshotCreate(BaseModel):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        description="Row objects to persist; values and order are stored verbatim"
    )


class SnapshotMetadata(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    created_at: str
    row_count: int


class SnapshotResponse(SnapshotMetadata):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


class SnapshotDiffEntry(BaseModel):
    row: dict[str, Any]
    count: int


class SnapshotDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    from_snapshot_id: int
    to_snapshot_id: int
    added: list[SnapshotDiffEntry]
    removed: list[SnapshotDiffEntry]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Retention policies and lineage-aware snapshot deletion
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class RetentionPolicyCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    retention_days: StrictInt = Field(
        ge=0, description="Non-negative minimum snapshot age in days"
    )


class RetentionPolicy(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    retention_days: int
    created_at: str


class SnapshotDeletionRequestCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    reason: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty reason for the requested deletion")


class SnapshotDeletionRequest(BaseModel):
    id: int
    snapshot_id: int
    policy_id: int
    reason: str
    status: Literal["pending", "blocked", "confirmed"]
    impacted: list[LineageSourceRef]
    created_at: str


class ConfirmedSnapshotDeletionRequest(SnapshotDeletionRequest):
    confirmed_at: str


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Retention exceptions (compliance holds blocking snapshot deletion)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


RetentionExceptionScope = Literal["version", "snapshot"]


class RetentionExceptionCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    scope: RetentionExceptionScope
    snapshot_id: StrictInt | None = Field(
        description="Null for scope 'version'; an existing snapshot id of this "
        "version for scope 'snapshot'"
    )
    reason: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty justification for the hold")
    expires_at: StrictStr = Field(
        description="Future ISO-8601 date-time including a timezone"
    )


class RetentionException(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    scope: RetentionExceptionScope
    snapshot_id: int | None
    reason: str
    expires_at: str
    status: Literal["active", "expired", "released"]
    created_at: str
    released_at: str | None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Processing tasks
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class ProcessingTaskCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    name: StrictStr = Field(description="Unique, non-empty task name within the version")
    depends_on: list[StrictInt] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Ids of tasks in the same version that must succeed first",
    )
    max_attempts: StrictInt = Field(
        default=1, ge=1, description="Maximum number of runs allowed for the task"
    )


class ProcessingTask(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    name: str
    depends_on: list[int]
    max_attempts: int
    status: Literal["pending", "running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    attempt_count: int
    created_at: str


class ProcessingTaskRun(BaseModel):
    id: int
    task_id: int
    attempt: int
    status: Literal["running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    started_at: str
    finished_at: str | None
    error: str | None


class ProcessingTaskWithRuns(ProcessingTask):
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


class ProcessingRunFinish(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    status: Literal["succeeded", "failed"]
    error: StrictStr | None = None


class ProcessingRunCancel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    reason: StrictStr = Field(
        description="Non-empty reason for cancelling the run; trimmed before storing"
    )


class ProcessingTaskDispatchRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    # Non-optional with a default: omission yields 1, while an explicit null is
    # rejected like any other non-integer ("given" values must be positive ints).
    limit: StrictInt = Field(
        default=1,
        ge=1,
        description="Maximum number of tasks to start; defaults to 1 when omitted",
    )


class ProcessingTaskDispatchResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


# Sentinel default for ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem.error: unlike the
# single-run finish payload, the batch item must distinguish an omitted error
# field from an explicitly supplied one, because a success item may only omit
# the field — writing it at all (even as null) is a 422.
ERROR_FIELD_UNSET: Any = object()


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    task_id: StrictInt
    run_id: StrictInt
    status: Literal["succeeded", "failed"]
    # Omitted for success, a non-empty message for failure. An explicitly
    # supplied value (null included) stays distinguishable from omission via
    # the sentinel default; the success/failure rules are enforced in the
    # repository after the path resolves so 404 precedence is preserved.
    error: StrictStr | None = ERROR_FIELD_UNSET


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    runs: list[ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem] = Field(
        min_length=1,
        description="Non-empty batch of task/run completions for the path version",
    )


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


class ProcessingTaskDependenciesUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    depends_on: list[StrictInt] = Field(
        description="Replacement list of ids of tasks in the same version; may be empty"
    )


ScheduleState = Literal[
    "running", "succeeded", "retryable", "exhausted", "ready", "blocked",
    "upstream_failed",
]


class ScheduledTask(ProcessingTask):
    schedule_state: ScheduleState
    blocking_task_ids: list[int]


class ProcessingScheduleResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    tasks: list[ScheduledTask]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Processing task run audit records
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class AuditRecordCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    event: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty name of the audited event")
    input_summary: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty summary of the input")
    result_summary: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty summary of the result")


class AuditRecord(BaseModel):
    id: int
    sequence: int
    event: str
    input_summary: str
    result_summary: str
    run_status: Literal["running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    previous_hash: str | None
    evidence_hash: str
    created_at: str


class AuditChainVerifyResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    task_id: int
    run_id: int
    valid: bool
    checked_count: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Read-only per-version processing audit report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class AuditChainProof(BaseModel):
    valid: bool
    checked_count: int
    # Stored evidence hash of the chain's final record; null only when the
    # chain is empty (it is still reported when valid is false).
    last_evidence_hash: str | None


class AuditReportRun(ProcessingTaskRun):
    proof: AuditChainProof


class AuditReportTask(ProcessingTask):
    runs: list[AuditReportRun]


class ProcessingAuditReportSummary(BaseModel):

The database file location is configured through the ``DATA_LINEAGE_DB``
environment variable so tests (and deployments) can point the service at an
isolated database. A new connection is opened per request and nothing is cached
in process memory, which keeps persisted data available across restarts.

        CHECK (source_dataset_id <> target_dataset_id)
    )
    """,
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quality_rules (

    """
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS

    ON snapshot_deletion_requests (snapshot_id)

    # A released or expired exception must survive the deletion of the snapshot
    # it named, so the snapshot link is intentionally a plain integer instead of
    # a cascading foreign key (mirroring snapshot_deletion_requests).
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS retention_exceptions (
        id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        version_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES schema_versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        scope       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('version', 'snapshot')),
        snapshot_id INTEGER,

        id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        source_dataset TEXT NOT NULL,
        source_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
        source_field   TEXT NOT NULL,
        impacted       TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at     TEXT NOT NULL,

    )

    # result) so that per-dataset invalidation stays a simple indexed delete.
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lineage_impact_cache_datasets (
        cache_id INTEGER NOT NULL
                 REFERENCES lineage_impact_cache(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        dataset  TEXT NOT NULL
    )
    """,
    # Audit records are an append-only proof chain: the database itself refuses
    # updates and deletes so the evidence history cannot be rewritten.
    """
    CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_processing_audit_records_no_update

    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'processing task audit records are immutable');
    END
    """,
    """
    CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_processing_audit_records_no_delete
    BEFORE DELETE ON processing_task_audit_records
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'processing task audit records are immutable');
    END
    """,
)


def database_path() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("DATA_LINEAGE_DB", DEFAULT_DB_PATH))


def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = database_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    # Schema creation is idempotent and committed independently, so every
    # request works against an initialized database file.
    for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:
        conn.execute(statement)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


@contextmanager
def db_session() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    conn = _connect()
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except BaseException:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def get_db() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """FastAPI dependency yielding a transactional database connection."""
    with db_session() as conn:
        yield conn

6	temporary location is enough to isolate a test.

application opens a fresh connection per request and reads the database path
from the environment at connect time, so pointing ``DATA_LINEAGE_DB`` at a
temporary location is enough to isolate a test.

from pathlib import Path

2467	def _graph_reaches_target(
2468	    graph: dict[int, list[int]], start: int, target: int
2469	) -> bool:
2470	    """Whether ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` along dependency edges."""
2471	    visited = {start}
2472	    stack = [start]
2473	    while stack:
2474	        current = stack.pop()
2475	        for dependency in graph.get(current, ()):
2476	            if dependency == target:
2477	                return True
2478	            if dependency not in visited:
2479	                visited.add(dependency)
2480	                stack.append(dependency)
2481	    return False

2484	def replace_task_dependencies(
2485	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,

2494	        conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
2495	    )

2500	        raise ConflictError(
2501	            f"Processing task {task_id} must not depend on itself"
2502	        )
2503

2505	    existing_ids = {row["id"] for row in task_rows}
2506	    unknown = [dependency_id for dependency_id in depends_on if dependency_id not in existing_ids]

2516	            "tasks can have their dependencies replaced"

2521	    # newly introduced cycle must pass through the target: it exists iff a new
2522	    # dependency can already reach the target.
2523	    graph = _task_dependency_graph(task_rows)

2527	        for dependency_id in depends_on

2531	        )

2533	    # Validation above shares this transaction with the write, so the replacement
2534	    # either commits atomically or leaves the graph untouched.

2537	        (json.dumps(list(depends_on)), task_row["id"]),
2538	    )

2545	def _schedule_states(
2546	    graph: dict[int, tuple[str, int, int, list[int]]],
2547	) -> dict[int, str]:
2548	    """Derive the schedule state of every task in one version.
2549	
2550	    Non-pending tasks map directly from their stored status (``failed`` splits
2551	    into ``retryable``/``exhausted`` on remaining attempts). Pending tasks are
2552	    resolved against their dependencies by fixed-point propagation: all direct
2553	    dependencies succeeded -> ``ready``; any dependency chain exhausted or
2554	    already ``upstream_failed`` -> ``upstream_failed``; otherwise ``blocked``.
2555	    The graph is acyclic (enforced at creation and on every replacement), so
2556	    the propagation terminates.
2557	    """
2558	    states: dict[int, str] = {}
2559	    for task_id, (status, attempt_count, max_attempts, _deps) in graph.items():
2560	        if status == "pending":
2561	            continue
2562	        if status == "failed":
2563	            states[task_id] = (
2564	                "retryable" if attempt_count < max_attempts else "exhausted"
2565	            )
2566	        else:
2567	            states[task_id] = status
2568	
2569	    changed = True
2570	    while changed:
2571	        changed = False
2572	        for task_id, (status, _attempt_count, _max_attempts, deps) in graph.items():
2573	            if status != "pending":
2574	                continue
2575	            if any(
2576	                states.get(dependency_id) in ("exhausted", "upstream_failed")
2577	                for dependency_id in deps
2578	            ):
2579	                new_state = "upstream_failed"
2580	            elif all(
2581	                states.get(dependency_id) == "succeeded" for dependency_id in deps
2582	            ):
2583	                # An empty dependency list vacuously satisfies "all succeeded".
2584	                new_state = "ready"
2585	            else:
2586	                new_state = "blocked"
2587	            if states.get(task_id) != new_state:
2588	                states[task_id] = new_state
2589	                changed = True
2590	    return states
